title: Tame extensions are dominated by unramified extensions of a uniformizer-root field
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$, residue field $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ of characteristic a prime $p>0$, and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $T/F$ be finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and let $C$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $T$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Assume that for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C$, its localization $C_{\mathfrak n}$ has ramification index $e_{\mathfrak n}$ prime to $p$ and finite separable residue field extension over $k$; here $\mathfrak m_RC_{\mathfrak n}=\mathfrak m_{C_{\mathfrak n}}^{e_{\mathfrak n}}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. There exist $m\geq1$ with $p\nmid m$, a finite separable extension $T'/F$ with an $F$-embedding $T\hookrightarrow T'$, and $a\in T'$ with $a^m=\pi$, such that, putting $F_m=F(a)$ and $R_m=R[a]\subseteq F_m$, the ring $R_m$ is a DVR with fraction field $F_m$, maximal ideal $(a)$ and residue field canonically $k$. For the integral closure $H$ of $R_m$ in $T'$, every maximal ideal $\mathfrak h$ satisfies $\mathfrak m_{R_m}H_{\mathfrak h}=\mathfrak m_{H_{\mathfrak h}}$ and $(H/\mathfrak h)/k$ is finite separable. No henselianity or completeness is assumed. Finite means finite-dimensional, and $F(a)$ denotes the subfield generated by $F$ and $a$.

source.place: Tag 0EXW, lemma-characterize-tame, implication (1) to (2); Tag 09EV, lemma-pull-root-uniformizer, for the root DVR and its residue field.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], the DVR $R$ is a Noetherian normal domain, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] makes $C$ finite over $R$. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], case (a), to the identity $R\to R$ and $P=T$: it gives a nonempty finite list $\mathfrak n_1,\ldots,\mathfrak n_s$ of maximal ideals of $C$, with DVR localizations and fraction field $T$. (For the fraction field, multiply a monic equation for $x\in T$ by suitable powers of $\pi$ to make $\pi^Nx$ integral.) Write $e_i=e_{\mathfrak n_i}$ and take $m=\prod_i e_i$. Each $e_i\geq1$ is prime to $p$, so $m\geq1$, $p\nmid m$, and every $e_i$ divides $m$. The residue classes of $m$ and $e_i$ are nonzero in $k$, so these integers are units in $R$.

source.place: Tag 0EXW, lemma-characterize-tame, (1) implies (3), choice of common multiple; Tag 09E8, remark-finite-separable-extension; Tag 09EM, remark-construction

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $T$ by [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique], and a root $a\in\Omega$ of the nonconstant polynomial $f=X^m-\pi$. Since $m\pi\ne0$ in $F$, the identity $-\pi^{-1}f+(m\pi)^{-1}Xf'=1$ proves that $f$ is separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. The minimal polynomial $g$ of $a$ over $F$ divides $f$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. To check separability of $g$ explicitly, write $f=gh$; the displayed Bezout identity becomes $1=g(Uh+Vh')+g'(Vh)$. Thus $g$ and $g'$ are coprime and $a$ is separable algebraic over $F$.

source.place: Tag 0EXW, lemma-characterize-tame, (1) implies (3), root extension; Tag 09H1, definition-separable (fields.tex)

proof.text: Set $T'=T(a)\subseteq\Omega$. By [lem-sfb-separable-generated-scalar-extension], applied with $K=F$, $M=T$, and $U=\{a\}$, the extension $T'/T$ is separable algebraic. By [lem-zl-separable-permanence] and the hypothesis on $T/F$, $T'/F$ is separable algebraic. The ring $T[a]$ is spanned over $T$ by $1,a,\ldots,a^{m-1}$. A nonzero element acts injectively on this finite-dimensional domain and hence surjectively, so it has an inverse; consequently $T[a]=T(a)=T'$. If $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ span $T/F$, the products $b_i a^j$, $0\leq j<m$, span $T'/F$, proving finiteness. The original inclusion $T\subseteq T'$ is the required $F$-embedding. Put $F_m=F(a)$. The same finite spanning set proves $T'/F_m$ finite, and [lem-sfb-separable-algebraic-intermediate-base] proves it separable.

source.place: Tag 0EXW, lemma-characterize-tame, choice of one field factor of the generic tensor product

proof.text: Let $A=R[X]/(X^m-\pi)$ with root $t$. By [lem-sbc-dvr-uniformizer-root-algebra], $A$ is a DVR domain with maximal ideal $(t)$. Evaluation $t\mapsto a$ maps $A$ onto $R_m=R[a]$. It is injective: its prime kernel meets $R$ in zero; if it contained a nonzero element, write that element as a unit times $t^r$ using the DVR valuation [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Primality would put $t$ and hence $\pi=t^m$ in the kernel, a contradiction. Thus $R_m\cong A$, with maximal ideal $(a)$. Monic division gives the $R$-basis $1,a,\ldots,a^{m-1}$, so $R_m$ is finite and faithful over $R$. Its fraction field is $F(a)=F_m$, since adjoining fractions to $R[a]$ first includes $F$ and then $a$. Finally $R_m/(a)\cong R[X]/(X,X^m-\pi)\cong R/(\pi)=k$, through constants, giving the canonical residue identification, and $\mathfrak m_RR_m=(\pi)=(a)^m=\mathfrak m_{R_m}^m$.

source.place: Tag 09EV, lemma-pull-root-uniformizer, root-algebra proof (also valid for m=1)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] to the DVR $R_m$ and then [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] to $T'/F_m$. The integral closure $H$ is finite over $R_m$. Every maximal ideal $\mathfrak h$ of $H$ contracts to the maximal ideal of $R_m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal]. Therefore $H/\mathfrak h$ is a quotient of the finite-dimensional $k$-algebra $H/\mathfrak m_{R_m}H$ and is finite-dimensional over $k$. Also $T'$ is generated as an $R_m$-algebra by the image of $T$: this algebra contains $T$ and $a$, and hence is exactly $T[a]=T'$.

Fix any maximal ideal $\mathfrak h$ of $H$. Apply [lem-sbc-dvr-normalized-compositum-local-diagram] with its $(B,A,E,F,C,S,Q,n)$ equal to $(R,R_m,T,T',C,H,\mathfrak h,m)$. Its finiteness hypotheses were verified in steps 1, 4 and 5. For every branch of $C$, the assumed ramification index $e_i$ is a unit in $R$ and divides $m$, and its residue extension is separable, exactly as the cited statement requires; that statement requires no divisibility condition on residue degrees. Its conclusion supplies a branch $\mathfrak n_i$, DVRs $U=C_{\mathfrak n_i}$ and $V=H_{\mathfrak h}$ with fraction fields $T,T'$, and a compatible injective local map $U\to V$. It also supplies $\mathfrak m_RU=\mathfrak m_U^{e_i}$ and the separability of $\kappa(U)/k$. All field maps agree on $R$, and $T'$ is generated as an $R_m$-algebra by $T$, as required. Every prime of $C$ above $\mathfrak m_R$ is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal], so the hypotheses on all maximal branches indeed apply to all primes quantified by the diagram lemma.

source.place: Tag 0EXW, lemma-characterize-tame, local branches in (1) implies (3); Tag 09EM, remark-construction

proof.text: Use [lem-sbc-dvr-abhyankar-local-maximal-ideal] and [lem-sbc-dvr-abhyankar-local-residue] on $(B,A,U,T,E,F,n,e)=(R,R_m,U,V,T,T',m,e_i)$. Step 4 gives $\mathfrak m_RR_m=\mathfrak m_{R_m}^m$ and a finite faithful $R$-algebra $R_m$; steps 1 and 6 give $e_i\mid m$, $e_i$ invertible, $\mathfrak m_RU=\mathfrak m_U^{e_i}$ and separable $\kappa(U)/k$; step 6 gives the compatible local diagram and fraction fields. The two conclusions are $\mathfrak m_{R_m}V=\mathfrak m_V$ and separability of $\kappa(V)/\kappa(R_m)$. For $V=H_{\mathfrak h}$, its residue field is $H/\mathfrak h$: a denominator outside $\mathfrak h$ reduces to an invertible element of that field. With the canonical identification $\kappa(R_m)=k$ from step 4 and the finiteness from step 5, this is exactly the required finite separable extension $(H/\mathfrak h)/k$. Since $\mathfrak h$ was arbitrary, all branches satisfy both conclusions.

The item's statement is exactly (1)=>(2) with e=m. Its hypothesis is Stacks' tame, and the extra word finite for the residue extensions is automatic. It uses a product instead of the lcm, which is allowed in the existential. No hypothesis was added or dropped and no conclusion was weakened. I checked all 7 steps against the cited statements. Step 1 applies normalization-structure case (a) with identity R->R and P=T, and the e_i are units. Step 2's Bezout identity -pi^{-1}f+(m pi)^{-1}Xf'=1 is correct, and the g|f transfer is correct. Step 3 uses generated-scalar-extension with K=F, M=T, U={a}, then permanence and the intermediate base; finiteness comes from an explicit spanning set. In step 4, evaluation from the root algebra (which allows n>=1) is injective, the fraction field is F(a), R_m/(a)=k and m_R R_m=(a)^m. In step 5, H is finite and H/h is finite over k. In step 6, every hypothesis of the sbc compositum local-diagram lemma holds; the condition on primes above m_R is reduced to maximal ideals by integral-prime-over-maximal. In step 7, the two local Abhyankar lemmas apply with (R,R_m,U,V,T,T',m,e_i), and kappa(H_h)=H/h. Edge cases T=F, m=1, several branches and equal characteristic all work. The DAG has no duplicate of this statement: lem-exc-tame-root-extension is the henselian case with an algebraically closed residue field, and the sbc tensor-factor lemmas need residue-degree divisibility. A traversal of 105 dependency nodes finds no cycle. The four generic sbc tools (09EV, 09EM, 0BRM x2) are correctly declared in tool_uses, and I accept them.
